title: Reusable SQS consumer: polling, concurrency, heartbeats, shutdown

user_story.i_want: a reusable SQS consumer that handles polling, concurrency, visibility extension, deletion and shutdown
user_story.so_that: each worker role only implements 'handle one message'

description: Define a `MessageHandler` trait whose async `handle(&Message)` returns `HandlerResult::{Ack, Retry(reason), Reject(reason)}`. The consumer long-polls (WaitTimeSeconds 20, up to 10 messages), limits concurrency with a Semaphore (default 4), and runs a per-message heartbeat that extends visibility every timeout/2 while the handler runs. Ack deletes the message. Retry sets visibility to a backoff based on ApproximateReceiveCount. Reject logs and leaves the message for the DLQ. On shutdown it stops polling, waits for in-flight messages (with a timeout) and exits. Health and metrics are on :8083.

acceptance_criteria.given: concurrency 4 and 20 messages taking 2 s each
acceptance_criteria.then: never more than 4 are in flight and all 20 are acked

acceptance_criteria.given: a handler running 3× longer than the visibility timeout (against ElasticMQ)
acceptance_criteria.then: the message was never redelivered meanwhile
the message is redelivered with a higher receive count
no new receives happen, in-flight work finishes and the process exits 0
